subject: physics
title: Evaporation and cooling
key_idea: Evaporation happens when the most energetic particles escape from the surface of a liquid. This leaves the liquid cooler. It happens faster when the liquid is warmer, has a larger surface or has air moving over it.

blocks.text: Particles in a liquid move at different speeds. This section covers how some of them escape.

items.meaning: The escape of more energetic particles from the surface of a liquid.

items: Some particles in a liquid have more energy than others.
A particle at the **surface** with enough energy can overcome the attraction of its neighbours and escape.
The escaped particles become a gas or vapour.
Evaporation happens at **any temperature**, even well below the boiling point.
Evaporation is the escape of the more energetic particles from the surface.
It can happen at any temperature.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Both turn a liquid into a gas, but they are not the same process.

items: Evaporation
Boiling

values: Any temperature below the boiling point
Bubbles of vapour form inside the liquid

items: Evaporation is at the surface and at any temperature.
Boiling is throughout the liquid and at a fixed temperature.

blocks.text: Evaporation cools the liquid that is left behind. The particles that escape take their energy with them.

items: The escaping particles are the most energetic.
The particles that remain have a lower average energy.
So the **temperature of the remaining liquid falls**.

blocks.text: (Supplement) A liquid on the surface of an object also cools the object.

items: The evaporating liquid needs energy, which it takes from the object it touches.
The object loses thermal energy, so its temperature falls.
Sweat evaporating cools skin, and a wet cloth round a carton keeps the milk cool.
Evaporation cools the liquid left behind.
An object touching an evaporating liquid loses energy and cools.

sections.heading: What changes the rate of evaporation

rows: More particles have enough energy to escape.
More particles are at the surface.
Escaped particles are carried away, so fewer return to the liquid.

diagram.alt: A predictor. Pick a change to a dish of water to see what happens to the rate of evaporation and why.
diagram.prompt: Pick a change to a dish of water.

options.label: Warm the water
results: More particles have enough energy to escape.

options.label: Cool the water
results: Fewer particles have enough energy to escape.

options.label: Pour into a wider dish
results: A larger surface area means more particles at the surface.

options.label: Blow air across the surface
results: Escaped particles are carried away, so fewer return to the liquid.

items: Warmth, a larger surface and moving air all speed up evaporation.
Always give a reason in terms of the particles.

checks.q: Describe evaporation in terms of particles.
checks.a: More energetic particles escape from the surface of the liquid.

checks.q: State two ways in which boiling differs from evaporation.
checks.a: Boiling happens at a fixed temperature (the boiling point) and takes place throughout the liquid. Evaporation happens at any temperature and only at the surface.

checks.q: (Supplement) Explain why sweat evaporating cools a person's skin.
checks.a: The sweat needs energy to evaporate. It takes thermal energy from the skin, so the skin cools.

worked_example.question: A pressure cooker is half-full of water. As the water is heated, some water evaporates before the water boils. Describe two differences between evaporation and boiling of the water in the cooker.
answer_points: Boiling happens at a specific temperature. Evaporation happens at a range of temperatures (any temperature below the boiling point).
Evaporation happens at the surface of the water. Boiling happens throughout the water.
worked_example.tip: One mark per difference. Compare both processes in each point.
